title: Exploiting the Lithosphere: Mining
seo_title: SSS 3 Chemistry: Exploiting the Lithosphere: Mining Worksheets (WAEC/NECO)
standard_code: SSS 3 Chemistry: Exploiting the Lithosphere: Mining
standard_text: The lithosphere as a source of minerals; mining and mineral processing: the extraction of gold with cyanide; extraction of iron and phosphates; the environmental impact of mining, including acid mine drainage. (summary of the senior secondary Chemistry curriculum, SSS 3; WAEC and NECO syllabuses)
meta_desc: Free SSS 3 Chemistry worksheets (senior secondary curriculum, WAEC and NECO): ores and mineral deposits, gold mining, exploration and mining, mining and the environment and ore grade and rocks. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: An ore is a rock from which a metal can be extracted at a profit.
key_sub: Gold is dissolved out of crushed ore with cyanide.
body_html:
How to think about it

The lithosphere contains the resources Nigeria's economy depends on: crude oil and natural gas, limestone, coal, tin, iron ore and gold. Gold is found in rocks and river gravels in states such as Zamfara and Osun; deep gold mines elsewhere in Africa reach several kilometres underground.

Gold ore is crushed and milled, leached with cyanide solution, and the gold is recovered with zinc or activated carbon. Iron is extracted from haematite by reduction in a blast furnace. Mining creates jobs and export income but also causes mine dumps, dust, loss of habitat and acid mine drainage.

Example

An ore has 5 g of gold per tonne. Gold in 1,000 t?

5 g/t × 1,000 t

Answer: 5 kg

Example

What causes acid mine drainage?

Pyrite + air + water

Answer: sulfuric acid formed from pyrite

Common mistakes

  • Thinking gold is mined as nuggets.
  • Thinking mining has only positive effects.
  • Thinking all rocks with metal are ores.

faq.a: It is very poisonous, so cyanide waste must be treated before it reaches rivers.

faq.q: What is done to old mine dumps?
faq.a: They are re-mined for leftover gold, or covered with soil and plants to stop dust and erosion.

items.q: What kind of rock is Kata Tjuta made of?
items.e: It formed from rounded pebbles and boulders cemented together.

items.q: Zainab asks how rock salt formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers
from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago
from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years
from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years
items.e: Rock salt formed from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago.

items.q: Nonso reads about a resource that formed from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago. Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how rock salt formed.

items.q: What is an ore?
c: rock containing a mineral in high enough concentration to be mined at a profit
a pure metal found in nature
items.e: Whether a deposit is ore depends on price and cost.

items.q: Bisi reads about a resource that formed from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries. Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how copper and gold ores formed.

items.q: Why is a cap rock needed for an oil or gas reservoir?
c: it is impermeable, so it stops the oil and gas escaping upwards
items.e: Shale and salt are common cap rocks.

items.q: Femi reads about a resource that formed from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years. Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how oil and natural gas formed.

items.q: Why are fossil fuels called non-renewable?
c: they form over millions of years, far slower than we use them
they are found only in deserts
items.e: Coal, oil and gas are non-renewable.

items.q: What kind of rock is the Organ Pipes in Victoria made of?
items.e: It formed from lava that cooled slowly and cracked into columns.

items.q: How did the rock of Kata Tjuta form?
c: from sand and gravel eroded from ancient mountains, then pressed and cemented
from layers of river sand pressed together
from mudstone changed by heat and pressure
from rounded pebbles and boulders cemented together
items.e: Kata Tjuta is conglomerate (sedimentary).

items.q: Why can a deposit that was not ore become ore?
c: a rise in metal price or a cheaper mining method makes it profitable
the metal grows in the rock
the deposit moves closer to the surface
items.e: Economics defines ore.

items.q: Dayo reads about a resource that formed from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers. Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how iron ore formed.

items.q: How does bauxite form?
c: intense weathering in a hot, wet climate leaches other minerals and leaves aluminium oxides
items.e: It is a residual deposit.

items.q: What is a placer deposit?
c: heavy minerals such as gold concentrated by flowing water in river or beach sands
items.e: The 1,850s Victorian gold rush was mostly placer gold.

items.q: Kemi reads about a resource that formed from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years. Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how coal formed.

items.q: How do oil and natural gas form?
c: remains of marine plankton are buried, heated and changed into hydrocarbons, which collect in traps
items.e: They need a source rock, reservoir rock and cap rock.

items.q: Usman asks how oil and natural gas formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago
from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries
from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years
from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years
items.e: Oil and natural gas formed from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years.

items.q: How did the rock of the Organ Pipes in Victoria form?
c: from mudstone changed by heat and pressure
from lava that cooled slowly and cracked into columns
from layers of river sand pressed together
from rounded pebbles and boulders cemented together
items.e: The Organ Pipes in Victoria is basalt (igneous).

items.q: Which method is used to explore for ore bodies by measuring small differences in gravity or magnetism?
items.e: Drilling then confirms the ore.

items.q: When is open-cut mining used rather than underground mining?
c: when the ore is very deep and narrow
when the ore is large and close to the surface
items.e: The Super Pit at Kalgoorlie is open-cut.

items.q: An ore contains 6 g of gold per tonne. How much gold can be extracted from 2,500 tonnes of ore?
Why is iron extracted in a blast furnace with carbon (coke)?
c: carbon is less reactive than iron
carbon is more reactive than iron and removes oxygen from the iron oxide
items.e: Fe₂O₃ is reduced to Fe by carbon monoxide.

items.q: An ore contains 8 g of gold per tonne. How much gold can be extracted from 800 tonnes of ore?
In the reaction 2[Au(CN)₂]⁻ + Zn → 2Au + [Zn(CN)₄]²⁻, what is oxidised?
items.e: Zinc loses electrons to become Zn²⁺.

items.q: Which steps are used to get gold from ore, in order?
c: crushing and milling, then leaching with cyanide, then recovery of gold
items.e: The ore is ground fine so that the cyanide can reach the gold.

items.q: An ore contains 8 g of gold per tonne. How much gold can be extracted from 5,000 tonnes of ore?
Which metal is extracted from haematite?
items.e: Haematite is iron(III) oxide, Fe₂O₃.

items.q: What is the lithosphere?
c: the layer of air around the Earth
the crust and the upper part of the mantle
items.e: Minerals are mined from the lithosphere.

items.q: In which kind of mining is ore removed from a large pit at the surface?
items.e: Open-cast mining is used when the ore is near the surface.

items.q: A mine extracts 25 kg of gold from 5,000 tonnes of ore. What is the grade of the ore?
items.e: Grade = 25,000 g ÷ 5,000 t = 5 g per tonne.

items.q: An ore contains 8 g of gold per tonne. How much gold can be extracted from 2000 tonnes of ore?
A mine extracts 1.2 kg of gold from 200 tonnes of ore. What is the grade of the ore?
items.e: Grade = 1,200 g ÷ 200 t = 6 g per tonne.

items.q: Which metal is extracted from bauxite?
items.e: Bauxite is aluminium oxide ore.

items.q: What are mine dumps?
c: large heaps of waste rock and tailings left after extraction
items.e: The dumps around Lagos are mine waste.

items.q: An ore contains 3 g of gold per tonne. How much gold can be extracted from 2,500 tonnes of ore?
A mine extracts 1 kg of gold from 200 tonnes of ore. What is the grade of the ore?
items.e: Grade = 1,000 g ÷ 200 t = 5 g per tonne.

items.q: A mine extracts 2 kg of gold from 500 tonnes of ore. What is the grade of the ore?
items.e: Grade = 2,000 g ÷ 500 t = 4 g per tonne.

items.q: An ore contains 5 g of gold per tonne. How much gold can be extracted from 500 tonnes of ore?
Why is cyanide used in gold extraction?
c: it forms a soluble complex with gold, so gold dissolves out of the ore
it turns gold into a gas
items.e: Gold dissolves as [Au(CN)₂]⁻ in the presence of oxygen.

items.q: Victor learns that an aquifer holds 1,200 billion litres. People pump out 10 billion litres a year, and rain refills only a small amount. About how many years until it runs low (ignoring refill)?
items.e: 1,200 ÷ 10 = 120 years. Pumping faster than refilling depletes groundwater.

items.e: 800 ÷ 25 = 32 years. Oil formed over millions of years, so it is nonrenewable.

items.q: What is mineral processing (beneficiation)?
c: crushing ore and separating the valuable mineral from the waste rock
items.e: Flotation separates many sulfide minerals.

items.q: How do fisheries quotas help keep fish stocks sustainable?
c: they limit the catch to below the rate at which the stock can replace itself
they increase the number of boats
items.e: Overfishing can make a stock collapse.

items.q: Ruth's town has 5,000 people. Each person makes about 5 kg of plastic per person each month. About how much does the town make in all?
Hadiza's town has 2,000 people who each use 3 kg of rubbish per person each day. If everyone cuts use in half, what is the new total?
items.e: Halving use per person halves the total, even with the same population.

items.q: Why is dust from mine dumps a health problem?
c: the dust makes rain more acidic only
the dust has too much oxygen
fine dust can damage lungs and may contain toxic or radioactive metals
items.e: Some dumps contain uranium and heavy metals.

items.e: Oxidised pyrite forms sulfuric acid.

items.q: What is rehabilitation of a mine site?
c: restoring the land after mining, for example by covering dumps with soil and plants
items.e: Plants stop dust and erosion.

items.q: Which rock is marble made from when it is changed by heat and pressure?
items.e: Metamorphic rocks form from other rocks.

items.q: Sandstone is heated and squeezed deep underground without melting. Which rock forms?
items.e: Metamorphism.

items.q: What type of rock is chalk?
items.e: Igneous: cooled magma or lava. Sedimentary: layers of sediment. Metamorphic: changed by heat and pressure.

items.q: A coal deposit has reserves of 200 million tonnes. If 30 million tonnes are mined each year, how long will the reserves last?
items.e: Lifetime = reserves ÷ rate = 200 ÷ 30 = 6.67 years.

items.q: How does sediment become sedimentary rock?
c: It is heated until it glows.
Layers are squashed (compaction) and stuck together (cementation).
items.e: Over millions of years.

items.q: How do metamorphic rocks form?
c: Existing rock is changed by heat and pressure without melting.
items.e: Marble, slate.

A coal deposit has reserves of 100 million tonnes. If 25 million tonnes are mined each year, how long will the reserves last?
items.e: Lifetime = reserves ÷ rate = 100 ÷ 25 = 4 years.
